details: Beginning study of toy_variance, toy_reduce_partial, and row-wise reduction ops as precedents for RMSNorm

Read toy_variance, toy_reduce_partial, toy_tilize_untilize, width_split, tile_reorder, row_reduce_accumulate fully. Key finding: SUPPORTED/INPUT_TAGGERS/validate/default_compute_kernel_config are the registry-model contract from tt_metal/third_party/tt_ops_code_gen/eval/op_template.py and eval/golden_tests/rms_norm/axes.py (imports rms_norm, INPUT_TAGGERS, default_compute_kernel_config from ttnn.operations.rms_norm) -- neither toy op implements this contract (both are single-core toys with no validate/SUPPORTED). No op_design.md exists anywhere in repo; template is references/op-design-template.md (no Blocking Model section in the template itself) but agents/incremental-planner.md mandates a Blocking Model section as first required section with exact table spec. Reported findings to parent.

Surveyed master.md Part1 and Part2 catalog; mcast_pipe.hpp and mcast_host.hpp (SenderPipe, ReceiverPipe, Mcast1D, Mcast2D); argmax_multi_core_program_factory.cpp as the production cross-core width-sharded reduce topology (unicast gather to a reduce core plus two semaphores plus a multicast turnstile); tensix_all_reduce example (reduce_scatter and tree topologies); shared_input_reuse.py plus test_mcast_pipe.py raw pipe test for worked Python ProgramDescriptor semaphore and mcast call sites; device-zone-scope-attribution.md. Note: perf_instrumentation.hpp does not exist yet in this tree, it is a planned distribution target named in that docs header; DeviceZoneScopedN macro and the 250 marker per RISC budget are documented in kernel_profiler.hpp and the knowledge capture doc instead. Also found that rms_norm op_design.md already specifies the full Lamp L1 contract for cross core width split combine, gather sum mcast via Mcast1D PerRow plus SenderPipe and ReceiverPipe, which is the primary actionable answer for this request.
